mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the prior quarter signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market that boosts wage growth and input costs, compressing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals a contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual shock of higher inflation and tighter policy, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average while personal income (PAYEMS) grows below its 12-month moving average signals a shift from spending to saving, implying weaker consumer demand and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) acceleration above 0.5% for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS QoQ growth > 0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly housing starts (HOUST) level above its 12-month moving average while industrial production (INDPRO) remains below its 12-month moving average signals a housing-led demand recovery with weak manufacturing, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.
